measurement_not_invention.value_statement: Mature Oregon white oaks are 50 to 90 ft tall and 24 to 40 in. in DBH
measurement_not_invention.source_excerpt: Size, Longevity, and Form Mature Oregon white oaks are 50 to 90 ft tall (120 ft maximum) and 24 to 40 in. in DBH (97 in. maximum).

measurement_not_invention.value_statement: European ash dominant and codominant height is 22 to 30 m at 48 to 120 years
measurement_not_invention.source_excerpt: Forest dominant/codominant height about 22-30 m and DBH about 0.22-0.50 m at 48-120 years, by site type.

measurement_not_invention.value_statement: V1's Laessig observation of 0.91 m DBH at age 100
measurement_not_invention.source_excerpt: At age 100 the composition gives 0.752 m DBH against V1's Laessig observation of 0.91 m, a 17.4 percent miss.

measurement_not_invention.value_statement: untreated fence posts lasted an average of 18 years before failure
measurement_not_invention.source_excerpt: In tests conducted by staff of the OSU Forest Products Department, untreated fence posts lasted an average of 18 years before failure.

measurement_not_invention.value_statement: the oak's 7.2 cm diameter at age 30 with one tenth of the decade change in squared DBH integrated each year
measurement_not_invention.source_excerpt: Oak DBH starts at E1 site class I's 7.2 cm at age 30. Thereafter G1's open-grown case sets BA and BAL to zero and integrates one tenth of its decade change in squared DBH each year, at Douglas-fir site index 35 m. The anchor and integration are composition choices, not measurements of a 30-year-old open-grown Garry oak.

measurement_not_invention.value_statement: the oak's reference height of 39.48 m at age 432
measurement_not_invention.source_excerpt: The script extrapolates the final height segment past age 200 for oak and 120 for spruce, and spruce DBH past 120. The derived-mature rows below expose those extrapolations; they are not published observations at 432 or 158 years.

measurement_not_invention.value_statement: spruce trunk diameter is twice the stand mean diameter of Wiedemann site class I
measurement_not_invention.source_excerpt: Spruce DBH doubles that class's stand mean diameter following Sterba 1975 via V1. Height retains the stand-grown proxy; doubling DBH does not establish an open-grown height-age curve.

measurement_not_invention.value_statement: the paper's rounded 2.8 cm of diameter growth per decade
measurement_not_invention.source_excerpt: Gould DBH uses the nearest integer year. Its worked 40 cm case yields 2.82 cm per decade, matching the paper's rounded 2.8 cm.

measurement_not_invention.value_statement: the oak's height and diameter below age 30, taken as a straight line from zero to the first anchor
measurement_not_invention.source_excerpt: Before age 30 both oak dimensions extend linearly from zero to their first anchor.
